passages.text: When a honeybee finds flowers rich in nectar, she does not keep the secret. She flies back to the hive and performs a dance on the honeycomb. Scientists call it the waggle dance. passages.text: Much of the salt we eat comes from sea water. Along flat, sunny coasts, workers build shallow square ponds called salt pans. Sea water is let into the pans and left under the hot sun. Workers rake the crystals into heaps to dry. The work is done in the hottest months, because rain would dissolve the salt and wash it away. That is why salt making stops when the monsoon arrives.

passages.text: All through May the fields lay brown, the dust rose up on every road, and the old well in our town held only mud and one tired toad. The farmers watched the empty sky, and the hot wind sang a dusty sigh. Then one June evening, dark and low, the clouds came rolling from the west. They rumbled like a drum, and so the birds flew home to find their nest. The first drops fell like tiny stones, then came the rain in silver sheets. It washed the roofs and cooled our bones and danced like children in the streets. Now frogs are singing in the well, the fields are green from end to end, and every farmer here can tell the sky has come back as a friend.

questions.prompt: What was the well like before the rain?
questions.explain: The old well held only mud and one tired toad.

questions.prompt: What came just before the first drops fell?
questions.right: Dark clouds rumbling from the west
wrong: Green fields from end to end
questions.explain: The clouds came rolling from the west and rumbled like a drum; then the first drops fell.

questions.prompt: The rain is said to dance like children. What does this show?
questions.right: The rain feels joyful and lively
wrong: The children are afraid of the rain
questions.explain: Comparing the rain to dancing children makes it sound happy and full of life.

questions.prompt: How does the mood change from the start of the poem to the end?
questions.right: From tired and dry to happy and fresh
wrong: From calm to angry and loud
From busy and bright to bored
questions.explain: It begins with brown fields and dust, and ends with green fields, singing frogs and the sky as a friend.
